findings.problem: Performance claim 'This is faster than the old implementation' has no benchmark, profiler, or measurement evidence. Rule 1 of PLUS max-performance extensions requires baseline workload, acceptance threshold, and before/after measurements for every speed claim.
findings.failure_mode: Performance claim is unsubstantiated; no named benchmark target, binary, or command evidence exists to证明 speed improvement
findings.fix: Add a criterion/iai benchmark measuring before/after latency or throughput with realistic input distribution, or remove the performance claim and replace with evidence of correctness only

findings.problem: rayon parallel iterator is used in what may be a hot path with no benchmark proof it beats sequential iteration. latency-throughput-playbook.md hard-bans 'Do not add Rayon because parallel is faster; require scaling evidence.'
findings.failure_mode: Parallel overhead (work-stealing scheduler, thread synchronization, Rayon veneer allocation) can make small/medium inputs slower than sequential iter(), yet no benchmark proves this workload is large enough to amortize parallelism cost
findings.fix: Benchmark sequential vs parallel with realistic input sizes; add evidence of thread-count scaling or document the minimum input size threshold where parallelism wins

findings.problem: SmallVec<[u64; 64]> is used without benchmark proof that the 64-element inline storage wins for this workload. latency-throughput-playbook.md says 'Do not add SmallVec unless inline capacity is justified by distribution and benchmark.'
findings.failure_mode: SmallVec adds SmallVec-specific branching and copy logic; if inputs are consistently small or the output collection is always heap-allocated anyway, the abstraction tax is paid for no gain
findings.fix: Benchmark SmallVec vs Vec for the target input distribution; if output is always >64 elements, SmallVec provides no benefit and adds code size

findings.problem: No latency budget is defined. The PLUS extensions require 'Track p50/p95/p99 or max latency when user-visible, real-time, networking, UI, or scheduler behavior matters' — this claim has no stated target, no p50/p95/p99 numbers, and no measurement methodology.
findings.failure_mode: Without latency targets and measurements, the performance claim cannot be validated or regressed against
findings.fix: Define latency target (e.g., p99 < X μs for N-element input), measure with realistic workload, and set regression threshold

findings.problem: No throughput budget is defined. The PLUS extensions require 'Track operations/sec, bytes/sec, requests/sec, items/sec, or frames/sec when batch, stream, or server capacity matters' — no such numbers exist for this implementation.
findings.failure_mode: Without throughput targets and measurements, the performance claim cannot be validated or regressed against
findings.fix: Define throughput target (e.g., > X million items/sec on Y hardware), benchmark, and set regression threshold

findings.problem: collect_even is a public API function with no test, no doc comment, and no proof of correctness. Rule power10_checked_results requires 'Validate external inputs at boundaries'. This function accepts arbitrary slices with no size bound, and no tests demonstrate behavior on empty input, single element, all-even, all-odd, or maximum-size input.
findings.failure_mode: No behavior contract is established; reviewers cannot verify correctness invariants without tests
findings.fix: Add doc comment with behavior contract, add unit tests covering edge cases (empty, single, all-even, all-odd, large input), and verify deterministic output

findings.problem: The function is 2 lines, which is below the <=25 line target, so this passes the letter of the rule. However, the brevity makes the performance claim on line 4 more suspicious — a comment claiming speed on a 2-line function that uses rayon + smallvec without evidence is a red flag.
findings.failure_mode: The function is trivially small but the performance claim is not trivially true
findings.fix: Either provide benchmark evidence supporting the claim or remove the unsubstantiated comment

missing_evidence: No benchmark target exists for the performance claim in src/lib.rs:4
No profiler evidence (perf, flamegraph) exists for rayon vs sequential comparison
No assembly/IR evidence (cargo-show-asm, cargo llvm-lines) for SmallVec vs Vec decision
No input distribution, workload size, or hot-path definition documented
No latency p50/p95/p99 or throughput numbers
No thread-count scaling evidence for rayon parallelism
No regression guard defined for the performance claim
residual_risk: Static review only; no cargo commands run. The primary blocker is that the stated performance claim 'This is faster than the old implementation' has zero benchmark, profiler, or measurement evidence supporting it. Rayon and SmallVec hot-path dependencies lack scaling and size-distribution proof respectively. The review cannot approve performance claims without named benchmark targets, baseline numbers, and after-change measurements as required by benchmark_proof and latency_budget/throughput_budget rules.
